# O'Leary Holiday Lighting — On-Site SEO Audit

**Date:** 2026-09-08
**Scope:** All 15 public routes served from `site/`, generated by `tools/build.py` from `tools/pages/*.html`.

## Read this first: the requested framing doesn't match this codebase

The brief assumes a prerendered Vite/React SPA with a `dist/` folder. **This repository has none of that** — no `package.json`, no Vite config, no `.jsx`/`.tsx` files, no client-side router, no `dist/`. It's a hand/AI-authored **plain static HTML site**: `tools/build.py` (a Python script) assembles `tools/pages/*.html` fragments into `site/*.html`, which deploys directly to Cloudflare Pages. There is no JavaScript framework anywhere in this stack.

Per item 1 in the brief ("if it isn't \[prerendered], stop and flag it — none of this matters until crawlers can see rendered content instead of a JS shell"): flagging it as instructed, but the underlying condition it's checking for — content is JS-shell-only and needs prerendering to be crawlable — **does not apply here**. Every route is already 100% static HTML with zero JavaScript dependency for content. There is no shell to prerender; the audit proceeds on that basis, with `tools/pages/*.html` + `tools/build.py` treated as "source" and `site/*.html` treated as the built/deployed output (the closest equivalent to a `dist/`).

All fixes below were made in `tools/pages/*.html` and `tools/build.py`, then built through `python3 tools/build.py` into `site/`, so they persist through every future rebuild.

## 1. Prerendering / crawlability — 100

Not applicable as framed (no SPA, no `dist/`). Every one of the 16 built pages (15 content routes + `404.html`) is complete, static HTML with the full page content present in the initial response — better than a prerendered SPA in one respect: there's no hydration step, no chance of a prerender/hydration mismatch, and no dependency on JS execution for a crawler to see content at all.

**Nothing to fix.**

---

## 2. Heading structure — 94

**What was already right:** every page has exactly one `<h1>` matching its actual topic (verified: 15 distinct H1 strings, zero duplicates — e.g. `roofline-lighting.html` says "Roofline Christmas Light Installation in Kansas City", not the site name). No level-skipping anywhere (H1→H2→H3 throughout, never H2→H4). `faq.html` already marks each question as a real `<h3>` inside the trigger button.

**P1 — FIXED.** The 5 service pages (`roofline-lighting.html`, `wreaths.html`, `tree-bush-lighting.html`, `ground-lighting.html`, `maintenance-storage.html`) each have a "Common questions" section where every question was a styled `<p class="qa__q">`, not a real heading — the one clear case in this audit of a heading-style element that wasn't real document structure (inverted: content that *should* have been a heading wasn't marked as one, unlike the FAQ page's own better pattern). Converted all 21 instances to `<h3 class="qa__q">`; the CSS rule (`site/css/site.css:1552`, class-only selector, explicit `font-family`/`margin`) applies identically regardless of tag, so there's no visual change — verified with a screenshot (`/tmp/shot-wreaths-qa.png` during this session).

**P2 — open.** `reviews.html` has no `<h2>` at all below its H1 (rating summary and review cards use `<blockquote>`/`<footer>`, which is fine, but there's no structural landmark for "the reviews section" itself). Not a nesting violation, just thinner outline than the rest of the site. Left alone rather than guessing at copy.

## 3. Meta tags — 92

**Before this audit, every page had a title and description and nothing else** — no canonical, no Open Graph, no Twitter Card, no `hreflang` concerns (single-language site, correctly not addressed). `viewport` was already correct. `<html lang="en">` was already correct.

**P0 — FIXED: zero canonical tags, zero OG tags, zero Twitter tags, sitewide.** Added to `tools/build.py` (`meta_tags_for()`, called from `build()`): `<link rel="canonical">`, `og:type`/`og:site_name`/`og:title`/`og:description`/`og:url`/`og:image`, and `twitter:card`(`summary_large_image`)/`twitter:title`/`twitter:description`/`twitter:image` on every page. No leftover Lovable/template defaults existed to strip (there's no Lovable/template tooling in this stack) — confirmed nothing hardcoded a `twitter:site` or similar.

`og:image` uses real, already-shipped marketing photography, not a placeholder — page-specific where a relevant hero photo exists (`roofline-hero.webp` on the roofline page, etc. — see `OG_IMAGE_OVERRIDES` in `tools/build.py`), falling back to `hero-house.webp` elsewhere. These are full photos, not purpose-cropped 1200×630 social cards, which is the one meaningful gap left in this category.

**P1 — FIXED: 9 of 15 titles over ~60 characters** (up to 89 for `maintenance-storage`), **8 of 15 descriptions over ~155** (up to 214 for `index`). Rewrote all of them; verified programmatically after the fix — every title is now ≤53 chars, every description ≤152 chars, and all 15 of each are unique (no copy-paste duplicates). Examples:
- `tools/pages/index.html`: title 86→53 chars, description 214→148 chars.
- `tools/pages/maintenance-storage.html`: title 89→51 chars.
- `tools/pages/roofline-lighting.html`: description 191→147 chars.

**P2 — FIXED: HTML-validity bug.** `tools/pages/index.html` line 3 (before fix) had a raw, unescaped `&` in the title (`"...Kansas City & Overland Park..."`) while every other title on the site correctly used `&amp;`. Browsers tolerate a bare `&` followed by whitespace, but it's invalid HTML and the kind of thing strict parsers/some crawlers can choke on. Fixed as part of the title rewrite (the new title also dropped the ampersand entirely by shortening).

## 4. Images — 70

**P0 — FIXED: a 733 KB PNG rendered at 61×53 CSS pixels.** `site/images/wreath-icon.png` (736×762 source, 733,331 bytes) was used as `<img class="wreath-accent">` in the homepage H1 (`tools/pages/index.html`) — `.wreath-accent` (`site/css/site.css:1327`) renders it at 61×53. That's roughly a 12× linear oversize and the single worst asset on the site. Resized to 122×106 (2× for retina) and re-encoded as WebP with Pillow: **7,906 bytes — a 99% reduction**. Updated the reference and added explicit `width="61" height="53"` to reserve layout space. Verified visually (`/tmp/shot-h1-wreath.png`) — no visible quality loss at display size.

**P1 — FIXED, partially: no `<img>` anywhere had `width`/`height` or `loading`.** Added `width`/`height` to the wreath icon and both logo instances (header: `123×81` matching the CSS-fixed size; footer: `161×110` matching the CSS `height:110px;width:auto` ratio), and `loading="lazy"` to the footer logo (below the fold on every page; the header instance stays eager, correctly, since it's above the fold everywhere).

**P1 — open, structural, not fixed.** Virtually all real photography on this site — hero banners, service tiles, carousel slides, service-card media — is delivered as CSS `background-image` on `<div>`s (grep count: 60+ occurrences across `tools/pages/*.html`), not `<img>` elements. This is a deliberate, common pattern for full-bleed/art-directed images with badge overlays, and it does avoid CLS (the containers have explicit CSS heights — `.tile{min-height:420px}`, `.hero--home{min-height:640px}`, etc. — so nothing shifts when the image loads). But it has real costs the checklist correctly flags:
  - **No native lazy-loading is possible.** `loading="lazy"` only exists on `<img>`/`<iframe>`; a CSS background-image is fetched as soon as its box is in the render tree, regardless of scroll position. Every tile/carousel image on every page currently downloads on initial page load, even ones far below the fold.
  - **No responsive art direction** (`srcset`/`sizes`) — the same full-resolution file ships to a 360px-wide phone and a 1920px desktop.
  - I did not rewrite this. Converting 60+ background-image usages to `<picture>`/`<img>` across 14 pages is a real markup and possibly CSS-layout change (background-size:cover/position semantics don't map 1:1 onto `<img>` + `object-fit`) that needs visual re-verification page by page — a follow-up worth doing deliberately, not as a drive-by inside this audit.
  - Several other photos are still 150–670 KB (`where-we-install-wreaths2.webp` at 672 KB is the largest remaining), used at genuinely large display sizes so not as clear-cut an offender as the wreath icon was, but likely still compressible. Not addressed individually — flagging rather than guessing at acceptable quality loss without visual review.

**Already good, no fix needed:** alt text is already descriptive and correct everywhere it matters — `alt="O'Leary Holiday Lighting"` on the logo, empty `alt=""` on genuinely decorative icons (wreath accent, the four "ornament" SVG-wrapped icons in the "One price covers the whole season" flow). No keyword-stuffed alt text anywhere. No `<img>` was missing alt entirely.

## 5. Structured data (JSON-LD) — 85, up from 0

**Before this audit there was no JSON-LD anywhere on the site.** Everything in this section is new, added to `tools/build.py` and built into every page.

**Design:** a single consistent `@graph` per page, not disconnected islands — `Organization` (`@id .../#organization`), `WebSite` (`@id .../#website`), and `HomeAndConstructionBusiness` (`@id .../#localbusiness`) appear with the **same `@id` values on every page**, so a crawler resolving multiple URLs on this site sees one entity, not fifteen unrelated ones. Page-specific nodes (`BreadcrumbList`, `Service`, `FAQPage`) reference `provider: {"@id": ".../#localbusiness"}` rather than repeating a flat copy of the business's data.

**Business type:** `HomeAndConstructionBusiness`. Schema.org has no more specific type for "Christmas light installation service" (`RoofingContractor`, `GeneralContractor`, etc. would all be actively wrong — this business explicitly isn't any of those); `HomeAndConstructionBusiness` is the closest correct, Google-supported LocalBusiness subtype.

**NAP data — what's real vs. what's deliberately omitted:**
- `telephone: "+19134268386"` — the same number shown on every page.
- **No `address` field.** No street address is disclosed anywhere on the site (only "Based in Spring Hill" + a service-area city list) — this reads as a deliberate service-area-business setup, not an oversight, so I did not fabricate one. `areaServed` (15 cities) is used instead, which is Google's documented pattern for SABs. **This does limit eligibility for some map-anchored rich results** — worth a deliberate decision from the client (disclose a service address, even non-public-facing, or accept the limitation), not something I should decide for them.
- `openingHoursSpecification`: Mon–Sun 08:00–20:00, taken directly from the "Hours: 8am – 8pm, every day." line on `contact.html`.
- `foundingDate: "2022"`, from "Local to Johnson County. Serving since 2022." (homepage) / "In business since 2022" (About Us).
- `sameAs`: the real Facebook page (`facebook.com/share/1JNp1tX1uM`) and the Google Business Profile short link (`share.google/d3Q3Bb9cU76evWhM8`), both of which are live links elsewhere on the site. **Deliberately excludes Instagram** — the footer's Instagram icon links to `href="#"` (`tools/build.py`, `.social__ig` — see §7), not a real profile, so adding it to `sameAs` would be fabricating a reference. Fix the link first, then add it to schema.

**AggregateRating / Review — scoped to visible content, with an important caveat:**
The "5.0 ★★★★★ · 44 Google reviews" badge is only actually rendered on `index.html` and `reviews.html`. `aggregateRating` (ratingValue 5.0, reviewCount 44) and individual `Review` nodes are added **only on those two pages**, and only for the reviews literally quoted on that specific page (3 on the homepage, 6 on `reviews.html`) — not a blanket copy of all reviews onto every page. I could not independently re-verify 5.0/44 against the live Google Business Profile (no live GBP access from this environment); this is what the site itself already asserts in two places, and it should be reconciled against the actual GBP number periodically, since a hardcoded schema value will drift out of sync as new reviews come in.

**Important, and worth being direct about:** since 2019, Google explicitly excludes **self-serving reviews** — a business marking up reviews of itself, on its own site — from the star-rating rich snippet in search results. Adding this schema is still worthwhile (it helps general entity understanding and is picked up by some other consumers), but **don't expect it to make stars appear in Google Search for this domain.** Real search-result stars come from the Google Business Profile itself, which this site already links to prominently — that's the correct channel for that outcome, not this markup.

**FAQPage** on `faq.html` (23 of its 24 visible Q&As) and each of the 5 service pages' "Common questions" sections, transcribed verbatim from the visible page content.

**One FAQ deliberately excluded, and why:** `faq.html`'s "What areas do you serve?" answer currently contains a live, publicly-visible `[CLIENT TO CONFIRM — final city list]` placeholder (see §6 for the full list of these). I left that question out of the `FAQPage` schema — baking a known editorial placeholder into structured data risks Google literally surfacing "[CLIENT TO CONFIRM — final city list]" as a search-result snippet, which is a worse outcome than the plain visible text alone.

**Service** schema on the 5 service pages (`roofline-lighting`, `wreaths`, `tree-bush-lighting`, `ground-lighting`, `maintenance-storage`), each referencing the shared `LocalBusiness` `@id` as `provider` rather than repeating business data — matches the brief's explicit "not a flat copy-pasted block" instruction. No `Service` node on `services.html` itself (it's a summary of the same 5 services covered individually elsewhere; adding a 6th overlapping block seemed like exactly the kind of redundant schema the brief warns against).

**Deliberately not added, with reasons:**
- **`Product`** — correctly omitted. Nothing on the site is a purchasable product with a fixed price; these are quoted services.
- **`priceRange`** — omitted. Numbers exist ($750/$500 on `faq.html`, "$200 and up" on `wreaths.html`) but no page states an actual *range*, and none of those numbers appear on the same page as the `LocalBusiness` schema that would carry them (`faq.html` isn't the business's core page). Approximating one would be inventing data not visibly stated as a range anywhere.
- **`HowTo`** — no genuine step-by-step guide content exists on the site.
- **`JobPosting`** — no careers/hiring page exists.
- **`WebSite.potentialAction` (`SearchAction`)** — no on-site search exists (confirmed: no search input anywhere in `site/js/site.js` or any page). Adding this speculatively would be exactly the "exists purely because a template included it" anti-pattern the brief warns against.

**What I could not verify (and did not silently mark "pass"):**
- **Google's Rich Results Test** — no outbound access to that specific tool from this environment. All JSON-LD was validated for well-formedness (every page's `<script type="application/ld+json">` round-trips through `json.loads()` cleanly — verified programmatically for all 16 pages) and checked by hand against each type's required properties, but that is not the same as Google's actual eligibility check.
- **Live GBP listing** — no access to the account. NAP/rating numbers used are what the site itself already publicly asserts, cross-referenced across the two places they appear (homepage hero, reviews page) for internal consistency, not against Google's backend.

## 6. URL & routing structure — 92

**Already good:** clean, descriptive, lowercase URLs (`roofline-lighting.html`, not `Roofline_Lighting.aspx` or similar). One consistent convention throughout — homepage is `/`, everything else is `/slug.html`, no trailing slash — matching internal links, canonical tags, and the sitemap exactly. **No slash-normalization redirect logic was added**, per the explicit instruction; Cloudflare Pages' native handling is left alone.

**P0 — FIXED (this session, before this audit): `sitemap.xml` didn't exist.** Now generated by `tools/build.py` (`write_sitemap()`) from the actual built page list — not hand-maintained — excluding `thank-you` and `404`.

**P1 — FIXED: `robots.txt` didn't exist at all.** Added (`write_robots()` in `tools/build.py`): allows everything, references the sitemap. Nothing on this site needed disallowing (no `/assets/`, no separate JS/CSS path that was ever blocked — there was no `robots.txt` to block anything).

**P1 — FIXED: no custom 404 page.** Added `tools/pages/404.html` → builds to `site/404.html`, which Cloudflare Pages automatically serves with a real HTTP 404 status for any unmatched path (its documented convention — a `404.html` at the publish root). Excluded from the sitemap.

**Not verifiable from source:** whether the live Cloudflare Pages project's "root directory" / "build output directory" settings actually point at this repo the way `functions/` and `404.html` need them to (see the caveat already in the assistant's prior turn about `functions/send-lead-notification.ts` placement) — that's a dashboard setting, not something in this repo.

## 7. Internal linking & navigation — 95

**Already good:** nav is semantic (`<nav aria-label="Main">` / `<nav aria-label="Mobile">`, real `<a>` elements, no `div onclick`). No orphan pages — every content page is reachable from the header nav, the footer, or a CTA button (verified by reading all 15 fragments' outbound links). Footer already links to all 5 services, About/Reviews/FAQ/Contact, and the top service-area cities.

**P1 — FIXED: no breadcrumbs existed anywhere.** Added a visible breadcrumb (`<nav class="breadcrumb" aria-label="Breadcrumb"><ol>...`) to every interior page (13 of 15 — all except the homepage, which doesn't need one, and `thank-you`, which isn't meant for organic entry), matching the real nav hierarchy: the 5 service pages show `Home / Services / {page}`, everything else shows `Home / {page}`. Matched by a `BreadcrumbList` JSON-LD node with the identical trail. Styled minimally to match the existing design system (`site/css/site.css`, new `.breadcrumb` rules) and verified visually.

**P1 — open, not fixed.** The footer's Instagram icon (`tools/build.py`, `.social__ig` link) points to `href="#"` — a dead link, present on every single page of the site. This isn't a template leftover from another tool; it's this site's own placeholder, presumably pending a real Instagram URL from the client. I didn't invent one. Worth fixing the moment a real URL exists — and once it does, add it to the `Organization.sameAs` array in `tools/build.py` (§5).

## 8. Performance (code-level) — 82

**Render-blocking:** one CSS file (`site/css/site.css`), loaded normally — appropriate for a site this size, no evidence of a large unused-CSS problem from reading it (it's one hand-authored stylesheet with page-specific selectors, not a bundled framework with dead utility classes). No JS framework, so there's no "code splitting of routes" to speak of — the static-multi-page-HTML equivalent (each page loads only its own HTML/content) is already the best case.

**Font loading:** already solid before this audit — `preconnect` to both `fonts.googleapis.com` and `fonts.gstatic.com`, and the Google Fonts CSS2 URL already includes `&display=swap` (which Google's API turns into `font-display: swap` on the generated `@font-face` rules). **Not present:** a `<link rel="preload">` for the font stylesheet itself — a minor further optimization, not fixed in this pass.

**Third-party scripts:**
- Google tag (`gtag.js`) — added this session per Google's own install instructions, `async` on the loader script.
- Feedbucket — already gated to the Cloudflare Pages preview hostname only (`tools/build.py`, `FEEDBUCKET` constant) and loaded with `.defer = true`; never touches the production domain.
- Google Maps iframe embed (`contact.html`) — already has `loading="lazy"`.

None of this is invasive. The Google tag snippet is the first thing in `<head>`, ahead of `<meta charset>`, because that's Google's own literal install instruction ("immediately after the `<head>` element") from an earlier request in this session. `<meta charset>` still lands well within the first 1024 bytes either way, so there's no real encoding-detection risk in practice — flagging the ordering as a technicality, not a fix.

**Not verifiable from this environment:** actual Lighthouse/PageSpeed numbers against the live deployed domain — no reliable outbound network path to run one from this sandbox. Everything above is a code-level read, not a measured trace.

## 9. Accessibility & mobile — 88

**Already good:** semantic landmarks throughout (`<header>`, `<main>`, `<footer>`, `<nav>`), `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls` on the FAQ accordion triggers, `aria-label` on icon-only buttons (menu burger, carousel arrows), `aria-hidden="true"` on decorative SVGs, `aria-current="page"` on the active nav item, a global `:focus-visible` outline (`site/css/site.css:75`).

**P1 — FIXED: no skip-to-content link.** Added `<a class="skip-link" href="#main-content">Skip to content</a>` as the first element in `<body>` (`tools/build.py`, `SHELL_HEAD_BOTTOM`), and `id="main-content"` on every page's `<main>` (mechanical change across all 16 `tools/pages/*.html` fragments). Styled to be visually hidden until focused (`site/css/site.css`, new `.skip-link` rules).

**Not independently re-verified in this pass:** actual touch-target sizing and horizontal-scroll behavior on a real/emulated mobile viewport. `site/README.md` already claims this was checked ("Verified free of horizontal overflow from 360px to 1920px") from earlier work on this site, but this audit's own visual verification was done at a 1280×900 desktop viewport only (see the screenshots referenced in §2 and §4) — I did not re-run a 360–390px mobile pass myself, so I'm not marking this a clean "pass" on my own authority.

## Everything changed this session, for the record

- `tools/build.py`: canonical/OG/Twitter meta tags, full JSON-LD `@graph` (Organization/WebSite/LocalBusiness/BreadcrumbList/Service/FAQPage/Review/AggregateRating), breadcrumb HTML + CSS hook, skip-link, `robots.txt` generation, `width`/`height`/`loading` on logo `<img>`s.
- `tools/pages/*.html` (all 15) + new `404.html`: shortened/uniqued title & description, `id="main-content"` on `<main>`.
- `tools/pages/{roofline-lighting,wreaths,tree-bush-lighting,ground-lighting,maintenance-storage}.html`: FAQ question `<p>`→`<h3>`.
- `tools/pages/index.html`: fixed raw `&`, wreath icon → optimized WebP with explicit dimensions.
- `site/images/wreath-icon.png` (733 KB) → `site/images/wreath-icon.webp` (7.9 KB).
- `site/css/site.css`: `.skip-link`, `.breadcrumb` rules.
- Rebuilt via `python3 tools/build.py`; verified: all JSON-LD parses as valid JSON, no unclosed/mismatched HTML tags across all 16 pages, all title/description lengths and uniqueness re-checked programmatically, visual screenshots of the homepage, a service page (breadcrumb), and the FAQ page confirmed no regressions.

## Open items for the client (not code fixes)

1. **Blue Springs and Lee's Summit** (both Missouri cities) are listed as service areas on the homepage (`tools/pages/index.html:382-383`) and About Us (`tools/pages/about-us.html:159-160`), but are **absent** from the dedicated, presumably-authoritative Service Areas page (`tools/pages/service-areas.html`), which only lists Johnson & Miami County, Kansas towns. This is a real content inconsistency, not something to silently resolve — only the client knows which list is correct. `areaServed` in the new schema uses the Service Areas page's list.
2. Multiple pages still have live, publicly-visible `[CLIENT TO CONFIRM — ...]` placeholders (full list: `about-us.html:164`, `contact.html:37,147`, `faq.html:311`, `privacy-policy.html:13,25,50,60,72`, `request-a-quote.html:140`, `service-areas.html:50,76`). These are intentional, per `site/README.md`'s own launch checklist — not a bug I introduced or should silently remove — but worth knowing that if the site goes live and gets crawled before they're filled in, Google can index that literal bracket text.
3. The footer Instagram link is a placeholder (`href="#"`) on every page.
4. No public street address is disclosed anywhere on the site; that caps structured-data eligibility for some address-anchored rich results (§5).
